key_insight: BenchX shows that cancer-detection AI can look strong on average while still failing badly in small, underrepresented patient and protocol subgroups.
clinical_relevance: This benchmark highlights the need for subgroup-level testing before deploying medical imaging AI, so performance gaps do not translate into missed tumors in real-world patients.
method: Built an open benchmark from 85,355 CT scans.
Evaluated 12 tumor-detection models across tumor size, location, demographics, and imaging protocol.
Used LLMs to extract and organize subgroup labels from clinical data for scalable analysis.
evidence_signal: Across the benchmark, state-of-the-art models performed inconsistently, with notably poorer results in rare or underrepresented groups such as young, female African Americans.
watch_item: Subgroup labels derived with LLMs and sparse case counts may still introduce uncertainty, so results should be interpreted as benchmark evidence rather than direct clinical performance claims.
paper_title: BenchX: Benchmarking AI Models for Cancer Detection and Localization with Demographic and Protocol Biases
